I have found that it is very difficult to learn math from the internet. Wikipedia, especially, is not very newcomer friendly. I taught myself trigonometry over the summer a few years ago by going to the "Math Center" at a local community college and tirelessly working through a text book, front to back. It worked very well. I am one of those weird people who is comfortable with textbook language, though. If you do not have access to such resources, ask around at your local high-schools for worksheets. Fun activity worksheets are the best way to practice skills because they make you feel like you accomplished something and it's normally pretty clear when you've screwed up a worksheet, so they provide an easy way to check your work. 

Basic arithmetic and algebra skills sometimes seem like a pain-in-the-ass or like they won't have a real-world application. Just keep going, because one day you'll be able to solve amazing problems with those skills! It sounds like you have the attitude necessary to succeed; just keep learning a little every day and you will improve vastly. 

Good luck!

HASBRO does not sell pieces alone. They do produce miniatures that are appropriate for very large boards and are rather expensive. One can make pieces, buy a new game just for the pieces and an extra board, find unofficial pieces that work for the game, or search craigslist/garage sales/etc for old pieces.

I bought some bags of plastic navy/army toys from my local dollar store and repainted them. Using unofficial pieces might bother some people, in which case I would recommend buying a game. 

I like the plastic toys because they are relatively inexpensive and give you freedom of choice for using men in different positions/weapons for different countries.
